CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for ongoing evaluation of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, headache symptoms, and medication review.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a significant improvement in his anxiety symptoms since the last visit. He continues to take sertraline at 200 mg daily and has incorporated lorazepam 1 mg as needed for acute episodes, which he has used sparingly, finding it effective during particularly stressful work presentations. He notes that anxiety episodes have decreased to approximately once per week, primarily triggered by high-pressure deadlines.
Sleep quality has remained stable, with Mr. Smith averaging 7 hours of sleep per night. He continues to take melatonin at 5 mg at bedtime and reports that the cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) techniques have become second nature, contributing to a consistent sleep schedule. He has recently begun practicing guided imagery as an additional relaxation technique prior to sleep.
Headaches have further decreased in frequency, now occurring once weekly with mild intensity. Mr. Smith reports that the combination of amitriptyline at 20 mg nightly and ibuprofen 400 mg as needed has been effective. He expresses a desire to explore alternative preventive measures, as he remains concerned about the long-term use of analgesics.
Fatigue persists but is noted to be less debilitating, with Mr. Smith attributing this to his increased physical activity and mindfulness practices. He has been attending weekly yoga classes and has made adjustments to his diet, incorporating more whole foods, which he believes have positively impacted his energy levels.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Melatonin 5 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 20 mg nightly 6. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed for acute anxiety episodes
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues his role as a software engineer, reporting that he has maintained effective stress management strategies through prioritization and delegation of tasks. He remains committed to his walking routine and has increased mindfulness meditation to twice daily, which he finds beneficial for his overall well-being. He has abstained from alcohol and reports that the plant-based diet has become a sustainable lifestyle change, enhancing his energy levels and overall mood.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Marked reduction in anxiety frequency; stable sleep quality; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Continued reduction in tension-type headache frequency; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, though improved; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted improvement.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily and lorazepam 1 mg as needed. Reinforce non-pharmacological strategies and consider a referral to a therapist for additional support. 2. Insomnia: Maintain melatonin at 5 mg at bedtime; continue to emphasize CBT-I strategies. Monitor sleep patterns and consider a sleep study if no further improvement is noted. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen as needed; assess efficacy of amitriptyline at 20 mg nightly and consider discussing preventive alternatives such as topiramate if headaches do not continue to improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue encouraging physical activity and mindfulness practices; consider a referral to a nutritionist for dietary optimization if fatigue persists.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-09-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
